---
title: "Empathy in Real vs. Synthetic Clinician Comments"
output:
  pdf_document:
    toc: false
    latex_engine: xelatex
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)

out_dir <- "../../output/3_inference"

qc <- read.csv(file.path(out_dir, "qc_comment_counts.csv"))
qc$match <- as.logical(qc$match)

results <- read.csv(file.path(out_dir, "inference_results.csv"))
summary_stats <- read.csv(file.path(out_dir, "empathy_summary_stats.csv"))

comparison <- read.csv(file.path(out_dir, "empathy_group_comparison.csv"))
comparison$significant_bh_0.05 <- as.logical(comparison$significant_bh_0.05)

kw <- read.csv(file.path(out_dir, "empathy_kruskal.csv"))

length_corr <- read.csv(file.path(out_dir, "empathy_length_correlation.csv"))
length_corr$significant_bh_0.05 <- as.logical(length_corr$significant_bh_0.05)

length_summary <- read.csv(file.path(out_dir, "comment_length_by_group.csv"))

# Everything below is derived from the data itself (group labels, mechanism
# codes, sheet counts, ...) rather than hardcoded, so the report stays
# accurate if the underlying data changes.
mechanism_names <- c(ER = "Emotional Reactions", IP = "Interpretations", EX = "Explorations")
mechanisms_used <- unique(comparison$mechanism)
methods_used <- results %>% filter(source == "synthetic") %>% pull(method) %>% unique() %>% sort()
group_levels <- c("real", methods_used)

n_sheets <- nrow(qc)
n_mismatch <- sum(!qc$match)
matched_sheet_names <- qc$sheet_name[qc$match]

# All downstream tables/plots are restricted to the sheets where real and
# synthetic comment counts match (see 1_xlsx_to_json.py / qc_comment_counts.csv);
# the CSVs already reflect this, but `results` (the raw per-comment predictions)
# needs filtering here too since the plots below are built from it directly.
results <- results %>%
  filter(sheet_name %in% matched_sheet_names) %>%
  mutate(group = ifelse(source == "real", "real", method),
         group = factor(group, levels = group_levels),
         length = lengths(strsplit(as.character(response_post), "\\s+")))

summary_stats <- summary_stats %>%
  mutate(group = factor(group, levels = group_levels),
         mechanism_label = mechanism_names[mechanism])

comparison <- comparison %>%
  mutate(mechanism_label = mechanism_names[mechanism],
         direction = ifelse(mean_synthetic < mean_real, "lower", "higher"),
         fold_diff = mean_real / mean_synthetic)

length_corr <- length_corr %>%
  mutate(mechanism_label = mechanism_names[mechanism])

sig_counts <- comparison %>%
  group_by(mechanism, mechanism_label) %>%
  summarise(n_sig = sum(significant_bh_0.05), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(n_sig))

describe_mechanism <- function(mech) {
  rows <- comparison %>% filter(mechanism == mech, significant_bh_0.05)
  if (nrow(rows) == 0) return("no synthetic method differed significantly from real comments after correction")
  paste(sprintf("%s scored %s than real (p_adj = %.3g, r = %.2f)",
                rows$method, rows$direction, rows$p_adj_bh, rows$rank_biserial_r),
        collapse = "; ")
}

ex_rows <- comparison %>% filter(mechanism == "EX")
ex_fold <- mean(ex_rows$fold_diff)

real_len_summary <- length_summary %>% filter(group == "real")
synth_len_summary <- length_summary %>% filter(group != "real")

sig_length <- length_corr %>% filter(significant_bh_0.05)
```

## Summary

Real comments score meaningfully higher than synthetic ones on
**`r mechanism_names["EX"]`** (`r sprintf("%.1f", ex_fold)`x on average;
significant for all `r length(methods_used)` methods, Kruskal-Wallis
p = `r format.pval(kw$p_value[kw$mechanism == "EX"], digits = 2)`).
**`r mechanism_names["ER"]`** and **`r mechanism_names["IP"]`** show no
significant real-vs-synthetic differences after correction
(`r sum(comparison$mechanism == "ER" & comparison$significant_bh_0.05)`/`r length(methods_used)`
and `r sum(comparison$mechanism == "IP" & comparison$significant_bh_0.05)`/`r length(methods_used)`
methods respectively). Effect sizes are modest throughout (rank-biserial
r = `r sprintf("%.2f-%.2f", min(comparison$rank_biserial_r), max(comparison$rank_biserial_r))`),
and comment length does not appear to be a general driver of these
differences.

## Data

This report is restricted to the `r length(matched_sheet_names)`/`r n_sheets`
source sheets where real and synthetic comment counts match. The other
`r n_mismatch` sheets (`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * n_mismatch / n_sheets)`) have
real comments merged into fewer cells than their stated "real breakdown"
total (several real comments appear to have been merged into one cell
upstream, in the source spreadsheet), which would bias the real-comment
group; there's no reliable way to recover the original boundaries (see
`1_xlsx_to_json.py` and `qc_comment_counts.csv`), so those sheets are
excluded here entirely rather than left in with mismatched counts.

`r nrow(results)` comments were classified: `r sum(results$source == "real")` real
clinician comments and `r sum(results$source == "synthetic")` synthetic comments,
split across `r length(methods_used)` prompting strategies
(`r toString(methods_used)`)`r if (length(unique(table(results$method[results$source == "synthetic"]))) == 1) sprintf(", %d comments each", unique(table(results$method[results$source == "synthetic"])))`.
Predicted empathy comes from three fine-tuned RoBERTa bi-encoder classifiers
(`r toString(mechanism_names[mechanisms_used])`; see `../2_training`), each
producing an ordinal label: 0 = none, 1 = weak, 2 = strong.

## Mean predicted empathy by group

Empathy labels are ordinal (0 = none, 1 = weak, 2 = strong).
The tests used throughout this report (Mann-Whitney U, Kruskal-Wallis,
Spearman) are rank-based. The means shown below implicitly treat the labels
as equally spaced, and are shown only as a quick, monotonic summary (see Table \ref{tab:means} \& Fig. \ref{fig:means}). The actual
label distribution (the ordinal-honest view) is plotted underneath it as
proportions per group (Fig. \ref{fig:sb}).

```{r summary-table}
summary_stats %>%
  select(mechanism_label, group, n, mean) %>%
  arrange(mechanism_label, factor(group, levels = group_levels)) %>%
  kable(digits = 3, col.names = c("Mechanism", "Group", "n", "Mean"),
        caption = "Population means per metric.\\label{tab:means}")
```

```{r plot, fig.width=6, fig.height=3, fig.cap="Average predicted empathy per population.\\label{fig:means}"}
plot_df <- results %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(ER_label, IP_label, EX_label), names_to = "mechanism", values_to = "label") %>%
  mutate(mechanism = sub("_label", "", mechanism),
         mechanism_label = mechanism_names[mechanism])

ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = group, y = label, fill = group)) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "bar") +
  stat_summary(fun.data = mean_se, geom = "errorbar", width = 0.2) +
  facet_wrap(~mechanism_label) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Mean predicted empathy label (0-2)", fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

```{r proportion-plot, fig.width=6, fig.height=3, fig.cap="Stacked predicted label proportions per population.\\label{fig:sb}"}
prop_df <- summary_stats %>%
  select(mechanism_label, group, prop_label_0, prop_label_1, prop_label_2) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("prop_label_"), names_to = "label", values_to = "proportion") %>%
  mutate(label = factor(sub("prop_label_", "", label), levels = c("0", "1", "2")))

ggplot(prop_df, aes(x = group, y = proportion, fill = label)) +
  geom_bar(position = "stack", stat = "identity") +
  facet_wrap(~mechanism_label) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Share of comments", fill = "Predicted label") +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Blues") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  )
```

## Real vs. synthetic (Mann-Whitney U, Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted)

```{r comparison-table}
comparison %>%
  select(mechanism_label, method, mean_real, mean_synthetic, p_value, p_adj_bh, rank_biserial_r) %>%
  kable(digits = c(0, 0, 3, 3, 4, 4, 3),
        col.names = c("Mechanism", "Method", "Mean (real)", "Mean (synthetic)",
                       "p", "p (BH-adj.)", "Rank-biserial r"),
        caption = "Mann-Whitney U test.\\label{tab:mwu}")
```

```{r kruskal-table}
kw %>%
  mutate(mechanism_label = mechanism_names[mechanism]) %>%
  select(mechanism_label, H, p_value) %>%
  kable(digits = c(0, 2, 4), col.names = c("Mechanism", "H", "p (Kruskal-Wallis)"),
        caption = "Kruskal-Wallis Test.\\label{tab:kw}")
```


Across the `r length(mechanisms_used)` empathy mechanisms,
`r sum(comparison$significant_bh_0.05)` of the `r nrow(comparison)`
real-vs-synthetic comparisons were significant after BH correction at $\alpha = .05$ (see Table \ref{tab:mwu}):

**`r mechanism_names["ER"]`:** `r describe_mechanism("ER")`.

**`r mechanism_names["IP"]`:** `r describe_mechanism("IP")`.

**`r mechanism_names["EX"]`:** `r describe_mechanism("EX")`.

The clearest and only consistent gap is in **`r mechanism_names["EX"]`**
(Kruskal-Wallis p = `r format.pval(kw$p_value[kw$mechanism == "EX"], digits = 2)`; see Table \ref{tab:kw}):
every synthetic method scored lower than real comments, by an average factor of
`r sprintf("%.1f", ex_fold)`x.

## Comment length

Real comments (mean `r sprintf("%.0f", real_len_summary$mean_length)` words,
median `r sprintf("%.0f", real_len_summary$median_length)`, SD
`r sprintf("%.0f", real_len_summary$std_length)`) are on average
`r sprintf("%.0f", real_len_summary$mean_length - mean(synth_len_summary$mean_length))`
words longer than synthetic comments and more variable in length. Synthetic
comments are tightly clustered around
`r sprintf("%.0f", mean(synth_len_summary$mean_length))` words
(SD `r sprintf("%.0f", mean(synth_len_summary$std_length))`) regardless of
method, suggesting the generation prompts constrain length fairly strictly.

```{r length-table}
length_summary %>%
  kable(digits = 1, col.names = c("Group", "n", "Mean length", "Median length", "SD length"))
```

```{r length-corr-table}
length_corr %>%
  select(mechanism_label, group, n, spearman_rho, p_value, p_adj_bh) %>%
  kable(digits = c(0, 0, 0, 3, 4, 4),
        col.names = c("Mechanism", "Group", "n", "Spearman rho", "p", "p (BH-adj.)"))
```

`r nrow(sig_length)` of the `r nrow(length_corr)` length-empathy correlations
(overall and within each group, per mechanism) are significant after BH
correction: `r if (nrow(sig_length) == 0) "none" else paste(sprintf("%s/%s (rho = %.2f, p_adj = %.3g)", sig_length$mechanism_label, sig_length$group, sig_length$spearman_rho, sig_length$p_adj_bh), collapse = "; ")`.
Length is not a strong general driver of predicted empathy: most
correlations are weak and non-significant, including every pooled ("overall")
correlation. Hence, the group differences reported above are unlikely to be a
simple length artifact, even though real and synthetic comments differ
somewhat in length.
